hook.line: Some things look great until you read the fine print. *A primera vista* is how you say so politely, and it always warns that a *pero* is coming.
hook.es: A primera vista parece una buena idea, pero tiene problemas.
hook.en: At first sight it looks like a good idea, but it has problems.

examples.es: A primera vista parece una buena idea, pero tiene problemas.
examples.en: At first sight it looks like a good idea, but it has problems.

examples.es: A simple vista no se nota.
examples.en: You can't see it with the naked eye.

examples.es: A primera vista el edificio parece nuevo, pero es muy viejo.
examples.en: At first sight the building looks new, but it's very old.

examples.es: A primera vista el plan parece justo, pero no lo es.
examples.en: At first sight the plan seems fair, but it isn't.

examples.es: A simple vista el café parece vacío, pero hay gente atrás.
examples.en: With the naked eye the café looks empty, but there are people in the back.

examples.es: A primera vista Tomás parece tranquilo, pero está nervioso.
examples.en: At first sight Tomás looks calm, but he's nervous.

rule:
*A primera vista* means "at first sight": an impression you have not checked yet. It sets up a *pero* that corrects it: *A primera vista parece…, pero…*.

Use *parece* (looks like), not *es*, because you are describing an impression.
*A simple vista* means "with the naked eye": *A simple vista no se nota*.
No article and no *en*: never *en la primera vista*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a fixed adverbial phrase: it works as one block, and you cannot change its small words.

readAndPick.es: A primera vista parece una buena idea, pero tiene problemas.
options: At first sight it looks like a good idea, but it has problems.
It is a good idea, and it has problems.
It looked like a bad idea, but it was fine.

readAndPick.es: A primera vista el edificio parece nuevo, pero es muy viejo.
options: The building is new at first sight, but it seems very old.
At first sight the building looks new, but it's very old.
At first sight the building is very old, but it seems new.

readAndPick.es: A simple vista no se nota.
options: It is noticeable at first sight.
Nobody sees it when they look closely.
You can't see it with the naked eye.

readAndPick.es: A primera vista el plan parece justo, pero no lo es.
options: At first sight the plan seems fair, but it isn't.
The plan is fair, but it looks unfair at first.
At first sight the plan is unfair, but it seems fair.

readAndPick.es: A simple vista el café parece vacío, pero hay gente atrás.
options: The café is empty, but people think there is someone.
With the naked eye the café looks empty, but there are people in the back.
At first sight the café is full, but it looks empty.

readAndPick.es: A primera vista Tomás parece tranquilo, pero está nervioso.
options: Tomás is calm, but he seems nervous at first.
Tomás is nervous, but he is calm at first sight.
At first sight Tomás looks calm, but he's nervous.

readAndPick.es: A primera vista parece caro, pero es barato.
options: At first sight it looks expensive, but it's cheap.
It is expensive, but it looks cheap.
At first sight it looks cheap, but it's expensive.

options: It is not a problem, but it seems like one.
At first sight it doesn't look like a problem, but it is one.
At first sight it looks like a problem, but it isn't one.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *A primera vista ___ una buena idea, pero tiene problemas.* (*parece* or *es*) At first sight it looks like a good idea, but it has problems.
yourTurn.answer: A primera vista parece una buena idea, pero tiene problemas.
yourTurn.why: It is an impression, so *parece* (looks), not *es*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *A ___ vista no se nota.* (*simple* or *primera*) You can't see it with the naked eye.
yourTurn.answer: A simple vista no se nota.
yourTurn.why: The naked eye is *a simple vista*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: At first sight the building looks new, but it's very old.
yourTurn.answer: A primera vista el edificio parece nuevo, pero es muy viejo.
accept: A primera vista, el edificio parece nuevo, pero es muy viejo.
yourTurn.why: First the impression with *parece*, then *pero* gives the truth.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: At first sight the plan seems fair, but it isn't.
yourTurn.answer: A primera vista el plan parece justo, pero no lo es.
accept: A primera vista, el plan parece justo, pero no lo es.
yourTurn.why: *No lo es* answers the impression without repeating the word.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: At first sight Tomás looks calm, but he's nervous.
yourTurn.answer: A primera vista Tomás parece tranquilo, pero está nervioso.
accept: A primera vista, Tomás parece tranquilo, pero está nervioso.
yourTurn.why: The true state of mind uses *está*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say about a café: At first sight it looks empty, but there are people in the back.
yourTurn.answer: A primera vista parece vacío, pero hay gente atrás.
accept: A primera vista el café parece vacío, pero hay gente atrás.
yourTurn.why: The *pero* part gives what you find when you look again.

yourTurn.prompt: Change it to the naked eye: *A primera vista no se nota.*
yourTurn.answer: A simple vista no se nota.
yourTurn.why: Only the opening changes: *simple* means the naked eye.

pitfalls.wrong: En primera vista parece una buena idea.
pitfalls.right: A primera vista parece una buena idea.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "at first sight", and Spanish keeps that *a*, not *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: A la primera vista parece una buena idea.
pitfalls.right: A primera vista parece una buena idea.
pitfalls.why: Almost. This set phrase has no article.

pitfalls.wrong: A primera vista parece una buena idea, y tiene problemas.
pitfalls.right: A primera vista parece una buena idea, pero tiene problemas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The impression needs a *pero* to turn it around.

personal: Think of a place or person that first seemed one way and turned out another. Say it: *A primera vista parecía… pero…*.
